newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer meets Waigel in Bonn - German ministry.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer meets Waigel in Bonn - German ministry.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer was meeting with Finance Minister Theo Waigel, the Finance Ministry confirmed on Tuesday.

The two were expected to discuss Bonn's plan to revalue the central bank's gold reserves, in a move which is believed would help narrow the federal budget deficit as it seeks to qualify for European monetary union.

Earlier, sources in Kohl's centre-right coalition said the government had abandoned plans to reap billions of marks (dollars) in quick cash profits from the Bundesbank in 1997 and would instead accept the central bank's offer to transfer the funds in 1998.

The humbling retreat will make it harder for Germany to qualify for Europe's single currency because the 10 billion marks ($5.8 billion) from the gold and currency reserves could have helped its drive to qualify this year for the Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria.
The agreement emerged after Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer met in Bonn, and deputies in Kohl's party expressed concern over the plan. ($ = 1.727 German Marks)
